title: Nvidia Leadership Uncertainty Meets 5% Treasury Yields
summary: U.S. equity futures weaken as Nvidia leadership uncertainty reverses part of Wednesday's AI rally; the 10-year Treasury yield returns to roughly 5% and the dollar strengthens. Verification pending: this edition is based on linked contemporaneous reporting, without independent claim-by-claim editorial sign-off.
reviewed_by: BLAQUE BAUX automated research; independent editorial verification pending

sections.heading: What Happened: observed facts
paragraphs: Reuters reported U.S. stock-index futures weaker Thursday morning, with the Nasdaq 100 futures down about 0.64% and S&P 500 futures down 0.31% in one premarket snapshot. Nvidia fell approximately 6% in premarket trading as reports emerged that its board was considering CEO Jensen Huang's future. No final leadership decision was established in the reporting.

After Wednesday's Veterans Day closure, Treasury trading resumed with the 10-year yield around 5%. The dollar held near a 19-month high as markets priced another Federal Reserve rate increase. Reuters reported Brent crude above $92 per barrel amid persistent Middle East supply risks.

Wednesday's technology rebound followed CoreWeave earnings and an announced shift toward borrowing facilities supported by customer contracts. A comparable Thursday morning snapshot of investment-grade spreads, high-yield spreads, issuer CDS and cash VIX was not independently established.

sections.heading: What Mattered: interpretation
paragraphs: The change since Wednesday afternoon is a reversal in Nvidia-led equity sentiment at the same time that bond markets reopened and Treasury yields approached 5%. The leadership allegations remain unproven; market repricing should not be confused with an established governance outcome.

CoreWeave's reported move toward contract-backed financing may lower its funding costs, but it does not establish that all AI infrastructure borrowers enjoy comparable terms. Higher benchmark yields and company-specific credit premiums can offset improving demand and utilization. Divergence between European equities and technology-heavy U.S. futures also argues against treating this as uniform global risk aversion.

sections.heading: What We're Watching
list: Any formal Nvidia board disclosure and measurable spillover into chipmakers, hyperscalers and AI infrastructure counterparties.
Thursday's Treasury reopening: two-year and 10-year yields, dollar strength and investment-grade/high-yield spreads.
Friday's U.S. producer-price report and its implications for December Fed expectations.
CoreWeave's contract-backed funding terms, cash conversion and peer refinancing spreads; separate customer commitments from debt-service capacity.
Brent crude and physical Gulf shipping developments; distinguish supply disruptions from changing geopolitical risk premiums.

sections.heading: Where We See Things Going
paragraphs: If leadership uncertainty is resolved without operating disruption and credit spreads remain orderly, a selective technology recovery becomes more plausible. If benchmark yields remain near 5% and financing premiums widen, capital-intensive AI infrastructure borrowers are more likely to underperform even with resilient customer demand. Available evidence does not support numerical probabilities.

signal: BLAQUE BAUX Signal: Wednesday's AI equity recovery is being tested by Thursday's governance shock and renewed bond-market price discovery. The more durable distinction is between suppliers booking equipment sales and borrowers able to fund capacity, service debt and generate cash returns.
